title: Unreadable foreign findings/marker records still abort runs (d9d's class)
description:
d9d fixed the checkpoint reads, but the same class remains on the sweep's other foreign reads: adoptRunFindings reads an ended sibling's findings via store.ForeignFindings and every other run's drafts under a key via ForeignFindingsByKey, foreignClaims reads every run's dispatch markers via ForeignAttempts (other epics' runs ride the same branch), and EpicPromotions/ForeignAbsorption decode foreign records too. One corrupt or newer-binary findings/attempt record — written by the same newer factory binary the absorbed finding describes — still aborts the boot or planning exactly the way the checkpoint did. The store already has the precedent for the fix (CheckpointHistory skips a version that does not decode rather than failing the read).
evidence: internal/reconcile/takeover.go:265 (ForeignFindings error aborts), internal/reconcile/claim.go:158 (ForeignAttempts error aborts), internal/runstate/foreign_findings.go:38 (s.load error aborts the whole list)

ticfac run epic-hn6 filed this backlog tick from the finding d9e14a71ac9991830038e2bb4404f7bc1b4aa7cdcad53c76f5387cdf52485e1e (reported by run-epic-hn6/tick-d9d/attempt-6): the done is reachable with the finding standing, so it is a backlog tick with an owner rather than the epic's to absorb. The decision record is .ticfac/runs/epic-hn6/absorptions/d9e14a71ac9991830038e2bb4404f7bc1b4aa7cdcad53c76f5387cdf52485e1e.json on the run branch.
